114: /// A tracked state of a¸ [`Once`] that can be used to ensure that the cell is

119:     /// The cell is occupied meaning it is being *written*.

143: /// A synchronization primitive which can nominally be written to only once.
144: ///
145: /// This type is a thread-safe [`Once`], and can be used in statics.
146: /// In many simple cases, you can use [`LazyLock<T, F>`] instead to get the benefits of this type
147: /// with less effort: `LazyLock<T, F>` "looks like" `&T` because it initializes with `F` on deref!
148: /// Where OnceLock shines is when LazyLock is too simple to support a given case, as LazyLock
149: /// doesn't allow additional inputs to its function after you call [`LazyLock::new(|| ...)`].
150: ///
151: /// A `OnceLock` can be thought of as a safe abstraction over uninitialized data that becomes
152: /// initialized once written.
153: ///
154: /// # Examples
155: ///
156: /// ```rust
157: /// static MY_ONCE: Once<i32> = Once::new();
158: ///
159: /// let value = MY_ONCE.get();
160: /// assert(value.is_some());   // unsatisfied precondition, as MY_ONCE is uninitialized.
161: /// ```

175:                 &&& points_to.id() == cell.id()
176:                 &&& points_to.value() is None
177:             }
178:             OnceState::Occupied => {
179:                 &&& v == OCCUPIED
180:             }
181:             OnceState::Init(points_to) => {
182:                 &&& v == INITED
183:                 &&& points_to.id() == cell.id()
184:                 &&& points_to.value() is Some
185:                 &&& f@.inv(points_to.value()->0)
186:             }
187:         }
188:     }
189: }

215:         let tracked state = OnceState::Uninit(points_to);
216:         let state = vstd::atomic_ghost::AtomicU64::new(
217:             Ghost((cell, Ghost(f))),
218:             UNINIT,
219:             Tracked(state),

227:         requires
228:             self.inv().inv(v),
229:             self.wf(),

231:         let cur_state =

233:             &self.state => load(); ghost g => {}
234:         };
235: 
236:         if cur_state != UNINIT {
237:             return;
238:         } else {
239:             let tracked mut points_to = None;
240:             let res =
241:                 atomic_with_ghost! {
242:                 &self.state => compare_exchange(UNINIT, OCCUPIED);
243:                 returning res; ghost g => {
244:                 }
245:             };
246: 
247:             if !res.is_err() {
248:                 let tracked mut points_to = points_to.tracked_unwrap();
249:                 self.cell.replace(Tracked(&mut points_to), Some(v));
250:                 // Extending the permission to static because `OnceLock` is
251:                 // often shared among threads and we want to ensure that
252:                 // the value is accessible globally.
253:                 let tracked static_points_to = tracked_static_ref(points_to);
254:                 // let tracked _ = self.inst.borrow().do_deposit(points_to, points_to, &mut token);
255:                 atomic_with_ghost! {
256:                     &self.state => store(INITED); ghost g => {
257:                     }
258:                 }
259:                 return;
260:             } else {
261:                 // wait or abort.
262:                 return;
263:             }
264:         }
265:     }
266: 
267:     /// Try to get the value stored in the [`Once`]. A [`Option::Some`]
268:     /// is returned if the cell is initialized; otherwise, [`Option::None`]
269:     /// is returned.
270:     pub fn get<'a>(&'a self) -> (r: Option<&'a V>)
271:         requires
272:             self.wf(),
273:         ensures
274:             self.wf(),
275:             r matches Some(res) ==> self.inv().inv(*res),
276:     {
277:         let tracked mut points_to = None;
278:         let res =
279:             atomic_with_ghost! {
280:             &self.state => load(); ghost g => {
281:             }
282:         };
283: 
284:         if res == INITED {
285:             let tracked points_to = points_to.tracked_unwrap();
286:             let tracked static_points_to = tracked_static_ref(points_to);
287: 
288:             self.cell.borrow(Tracked(static_points_to)).as_ref()
289:         } else {
290:             None
291:         }
292:     }
293: }

298: /// a wrapper [`AtomicDataWithOwner<V, Own>`] where `Own` is the
299: /// permission type so that we can reason about non-trivial runtime
300: /// properties in verification.
301: pub type Once<V, Own, F> = OnceImpl<AtomicDataWithOwner<V, Own>, F>;

14: `PCell<T>` (which stands for "permissioned cell") is the most primitive Verus `Cell` type.
15: It can often be used as a replacement for Rust's [`UnsafeCell`], and it can serve
16: as a basis for verifying many other interior-mutable types
17: (e.g., [`InvCell`](super::invcell::InvCell),
18: [`RefCell`](https://github.com/verus-lang/verus/blob/main/examples/state_machines/tutorial/ref_cell.rs)).

20: `PCell` uses a _ghost permission token_ similar to [`simple_pptr::PPtr`](super::super::simple_pptr) -- see the [`simple_pptr::PPtr`](super::super::simple_pptr)
21: documentation for the basics.
22: For `PCell`, the associated type of the permission token is [`PointsTo`].
23: 
24: If you want a cell that can be optionally initialized, see [`pcell_maybe_uninit::PCell`](super::pcell_maybe_uninit::PCell).
25: 
26: ### Differences from `PPtr`.
27: 
28: Whereas [`simple_pptr::PPtr`](super::super::simple_pptr) represents a fixed address in memory,
29: a `PCell` has _no_ fixed address because a `PCell` might be moved.
30: As such, the [`pcell.id()`](PCell::id) does not correspond to a memory address; rather,
31: it is a unique identifier that is fixed for a given cell, even when it is moved.
32: 
33: The arbitrary ID given by [`pcell.id()`](PCell::id) is of type [`CellId`].
34: Despite the fact that it is, in some ways, "like a pointer", note that
35: `CellId` does not support any meangingful "pointer arithmetic,"
36: has no concept of a "null ID",
37: and has no runtime representation.
38: 
39: ### Differences from [`UnsafeCell`](core::cell::UnsafeCell).
40: 
41: Though inspired by `UnsafeCell`, `PCell` is not quite the same thing.
42: The differences include:
43: 
44:  * `PCell<T>` **does not call the destructor of `T` when it goes out of scope**.
45:    Technically speaking, `PCell<T>` is actually implemented via
46:    `ManuallyDrop<UnsafeCell<T>>`. This is because dropping the contents is unsound
47:    if the `PointsTo<T>` is not also reclaimed. To drop a `PCell<T>` without leaking,
48:    call [`into_inner`](Self::into_inner) with the corresponding `PointsTo`.
49: 
50:  * `PCell<T>` _always_ implements `Send` and `Sync`, regardless of the type `T`.
51:    Instead, it is `PointsTo<T>` where the marker traits matter.
52:    (It doesn't matter if you move the bytes to another thread if you can't access them.)
